First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}-{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,(x){|}_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}-{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡(4\cdot \frac{{e}^{3}}{4})\,(\frac{{e}^{3}}{4})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(4\cdot \frac{1}{4})\,(\frac{1}{4})]-{\int }_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-x{|}_{1/4}^{{e}^{3}/4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{e}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{3}+\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(2{e}^{3}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
